newsitem.title: UK: China plans 500 mln mark Eurobond in June-bankers.
newsitem.headline: China plans 500 mln mark Eurobond in June-bankers.

text.p: China plans to launch a 500 million mark five-year Eurobond in June, bankers familiar with the transaction said on Tuesday.
"China's bond is due in around two weeks," a Frankfurt-based syndicate manager said.
"We are expecting a 500 million five-year deal, and pricing is likely to be in line with where its dollar paper is trading," he said.
Dealers said this would offer a spread in the mid-50s basis points to 60 b.p. over German government bonds.
Last week, the official Chinese Xinhua news agency said the mark Eurobond would be underwritten by Credit Suisse First Boston and Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.
It said the bond would be issued by the Ministry of Finance on behalf of the Chinese government.
In June last year China launched a $700 million five-year global bond via CSFB and Morgan Stanley. The deal was priced to yield 80 b.p. over U.S. Treasury notes.
China is rated A3 by Moody's Investors Service and BBB by Standard & Poor's Corp.
